findings.title: Denial as rejection of a beneficent order
findings.claim: The clause's denial can be heard as rejection of a good that becomes real in benefiting another, so the rejected good is an operative beneficent order rather than only a detached value.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb كَذَّبَ carries content-directed rejection through بِ, while ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ carries both the valued-good facet and the beneficent-action facet; the supplied 92:18 giving connection makes those focus carriers meet a concrete action that benefits and purifies.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the good being rejected has practical shape: it is a value that is made visible through giving, not merely a pleasant or abstract description.
findings.containment: The ordinary reading remains that the subject denies the good; this is a contextual beneficent-order resonance and does not turn the noun into a general translation for charity or import a wider moral thesis.

epistemic.reason: A trusted cross-run finding is corroborated by two legacy reader-walk records and an exact supplied giving connection, while the relation between the focus denial and the beneficent order remains an inference.
